ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a two-port network, with the left port labeled 1 and 1′, and the right port labeled 2 and 2′. Voltmeter V1 is connected between the upper and lower terminals of the left port, with polarity upper terminal “+” and lower terminal “-”; voltmeter V2 is connected between the upper and lower terminals of the right port, with the same polarity of upper terminal “+” and lower terminal “-”. On the left side, a 6 V DC source, ideal ammeter A1, and switch S1 are externally connected, and S1 controls the current path of the left port; on the right side, a 1.5 V DC source, ideal ammeter A2, and switch S2 are externally connected, and S2 controls the current path of the right port. Reasoning: The two-port z parameters are defined as V1 = z11 I1 + z12 I2, V2 = z21 I1 + z22 I2. According to the readings given in the problem, when S1 is open and S2 is closed, the left port is open-circuited, so I1 = A1 = 0; the right port current I2 = A2 = 1 A, and V1 = 4.5 V, V2 = 1.5 V. Therefore under the condition I1 = 0, z12 = V1/I2 = 4.5/1 = 4.5, z22 = V2/I2 = 1.5/1 = 1.5. When S1 is closed and S2 is open, the right port is open-circuited, so I2 = A2 = 0; the left port current I1 = A1 = 4 A, and V1 = 6 V, V2 = 6 V. Therefore under the condition I2 = 0, z11 = V1/I1 = 6/4 = 1.5, z21 = V2/I1 = 6/4 = 1.5. Arranged according to [[z11, z12], [z21, z22]], the z-parameter matrix is obtained.
